## Appearance

Anne is a tall, slender girl with a pointed chin, an oval cheek, and milk-white skin, though her face and nose have historically borne freckles. Her hair, which is famously red, has been worn in long braids, shingled closely, and cut into short silky curls. It is also described by some as auburn or glossy, occasionally loosening into rings around her neck and forehead. She has big, luminous gray eyes that are sometimes characterized as gray-green, set against cheeks that faint flushed with pink.

## Personality

Characterized by an imaginative, passionate, and serious-minded nature, she is known for her romantic worldview and a tendency to fall into daydreams. Although recognized as smart, obedient, and strong-willed, she reflects on having been heedless and impulsive in her youth. She possesses a creative gift for storytelling and writing fanciful, fairylike pieces, alongside a natural affinity for working with children. Driven by academic ambition, she has sought to win scholarships, attend college, and perform well to bring pride to those around her. Additionally, her desire to add beauty to life is paired with a deep, earnest loyalty to her friends. Despite her wisdom and maturity, she retains a youthful spirit inside.

## History

Brought home to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) by [Matthew Cuthbert](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md), young orphan Anne Shirley broke down upon learning that [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) expected a boy, but [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) ultimately agreed to raise her. Anne formed an instant, lifelong bond with her neighbor [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md), though she suffered several dramatic early blunders, including accidentally getting [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) drunk on currant wine and later being forced to cut her hair short after dyeing it green. Her passionate temper flared when [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) teased her red hair, sparking a intense academic rivalry that lasted through their shared preparation for the Queen's [Entrance](../codex/places.md#entrance) examination. Following Matthew's sudden death from a heart attack, Anne gave up her prestigious college scholarship to stay at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) to care for [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) and teach locally, during which time she and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) finally ended their feud and became close friends. After earning her degree at [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college) and declining marriage proposals from other suitors, Anne happily accepted Gilbert's proposal in [Hester](../character/hester-gray.md) Gray's garden. Upon marrying, the couple moved into a small house at [Four Winds Harbor](../codex/places.md#four-winds-harbor), where Anne endured the tragic loss of her firstborn infant daughter, Joyce, before giving birth to a healthy son named James Matthew. Over time, the family expanded and relocated to a larger home in [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) St. Mary called [Ingleside](../codex/places.md#ingleside), where Anne managed her bustling household alongside her loyal housekeeper [Susan Baker](../character/susan.md). Though her later years were defined by raising her children and participating in local village affairs, Anne remained a loving, supportive mother when her son Walter engaged in a physical fight to defend her honor.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P1](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0001), [v1 CHAPTER III. ## Quotes

> "Pretty well. I imagine a good deal, and that helps to pass the time. Of course, it’s rather lonesome. But then, I may as well get used to that."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P11](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0011)

> "I don’t get cross about other things; but I’m so tired of being twitted about my hair and it just makes me boil right over. Do you suppose my hair will really be a handsome auburn when I grow up?"
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P43](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0043)

> "I love pretty things; and I hate to look in the glass and see something that isn’t pretty. It makes me feel so sorrowful—just as I feel when I look at any ugly thing. I pity it because it isn’t beautiful."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P45](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0045)

> "I love Green Gables already, and I never loved any place before. No place ever seemed like home. Oh, Marilla, I’m so happy. I could pray right now and not find it a bit hard."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P49](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0049)

> "Oh, Marilla, I’m frightened—now that it has come I’m actually frightened. What if she shouldn’t like me! It would be the most tragical disappointment of my life."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P10](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0010)
